Amity

AM-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Amity is a friendly, peaceful relationship, especially between nations or groups.

Years after the messy divorce, the two families surprised everyone by celebrating the holidays together in genuine amity.

Worked Example

The treaty established a lasting amity between the two former enemies, opening trade routes that had been closed for a generation.

Amity describes friendliness on a larger, often formal scale -- between nations, towns, or groups -- rather than a single close friendship.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

friendship: Friendship is the personal bond between individuals who know and enjoy each other -- it lives between people. Amity is friendliness on a larger, more formal scale: nations, towns, or rival groups getting along peacefully. You have a friendship with a classmate; two countries maintain amity.

goodwill: Goodwill is the friendly, generous feeling one side holds toward another -- an attitude inside someone. Amity is the peaceful, friendly relationship itself, the state existing between two sides. Goodwill is what each government feels; amity is what the two governments share.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

hostility: unfriendly or antagonistic behavior

enmity: a deep, mutual hatred or hostility

Where it sits · how warm the relationship is — civility → amity → brotherhood

civility vs. amity: Civility is simply polite, respectful behavior, without the warm friendliness of true amity.

brotherhood vs. amity: Brotherhood runs warmer and deeper than amity: not just friendly, peaceful dealings between two sides, but a bond so close they treat each other as family.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — am-

root — am-: to love, to be a friend to (Latin amare / amicus)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Amity comes from Latin amicus ('friend'), from amare ('to love') -- the same root behind the everyday word amiable ('friendly and pleasant'). Add -ity and you get 'the state of being friendly.'

Use the root in a new word: amiable

Use the root in a new word: amiable: The new neighbor turned out to be an amiable man who waved at everyone on his morning walk.
